title: Understanding Bag-of-Words Encoding
text: Bag-of-words encoding is typically used for text data. It involves creating a vector representation of text by counting the frequency of each word in a document. How might this apply to numerical data like age?

title: Consider the Nature of Age Data
text: Age is a continuous numerical variable. Think about how you can transform or encode this type of data to be useful in a linear model.

title: Possible Transformations for Age
text: Consider transformations such as normalization, standardization, or binning. How might these help in capturing the meaning of age in the model?

title: Encoding Age for Linear Models
text: One way to encode age is by normalizing it to a range between $$0$$ and $$1$$. This can be done using the formula: $$\frac{age-\operatorname{min}\left(age\right)}{\operatorname{max}\left(age\right)-\operatorname{min}\left(age\right)}$$.

title: Binning Age Data
text: Another approach is to bin the age data into categories, such as $$'18-25'$$, $$'26-35'$$, etc. This can be useful if age has a non-linear relationship with the target variable.
